page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, this instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system features a substantial memory capacity of 432.0 GB, translating to 13.5 GB of RAM per core, and includes 885 GB of local SSD storage. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by weak single-core capabilities but stable multi-core execution. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the lower clock speed and older architecture of the Broadwell-generation CPU. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including PassMark CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, achieve average tier performance. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads also register in the middle 50%, supporting the server's capacity to handle large datasets despite the single-threaded processing limitations.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded throughput, this server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications rather than compute-heavy tasks. It is well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale data processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a viable choice for workloads where RAM capacity is the primary constraint and ultra-high single-core performance is not required.

Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff: single-core benchmarks for CPU and text processing rank in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently achieve average tier results. This hardware profile makes the instance highly suitable for memory-bound workloads, such as relational databases, Redis caching, and multi-threaded enterprise applications, offering a balanced resource density for environments where memory capacity is prioritized over raw single-threaded compute speed.
